rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for joining a queue or forming a line.

example.english: We queue at the bank in the morning to withdraw money.
example.traditional: 我哋朝早去銀行排隊攞錢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 ziu1 zou2 heoi3 ngan4 hong4 paai4 deoi6 lo2 cin2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for a queue of people, vehicles, or other things.

example.english: The cars formed a queue at the tunnel entrance.
example.traditional: 啲車喺隧道口排成一隊。
example.jyutping: dik1 ce1 hai2 seoi6 dou6 hau2 paai4 sing4 jat1 deoi6

rows.note: Use this specifically for a long visible line of people, especially one described as stretching out.

example.english: Before the concert started, a long queue of people had already formed outside.
example.traditional: 演唱會未開場，場外已經排咗條人龍。
example.jyutping: jin2 coeng3 wui6 mei6 hoi1 coeng4 coeng4 ngoi6 ji5 ging1 paai4 zo2 tiu4 jan4 lung4

rows.note: Use this for a waiting list that organizes applicants or items by their turn.

example.english: To apply for a dormitory, you must first join the queue; you will be notified when a place is available.
example.traditional: 申請宿舍要先登記入輪候名單，有位先會通知你。
example.jyutping: san1 cing2 suk1 se3 jiu3 sin1 dang1 gei3 jap6 leon4 hau6 ming4 daan1 jau5 wai2 sin1 wui5 tung1 zi1 nei5
